# OpenC 1.0.0

OpenC 1.0.0 is the first final release for the supported Windows x86-64
Hosted scope.

Highlights:

- the compiler is written in OpenC and reaches a byte-identical native fixed
  point;
- normal compilation directly emits PE32+ without generated C, TinyCC, D,
  Python, a C runtime, an assembler, or an external linker;
- 278/278 authored conformance fixtures pass;
- the fully validating self-build remains inside the 25-second and 64 MiB
  working-set gates;
- the standalone and source archives are built twice and compared byte for
  byte;
- the dependency-free VS Code extension embeds the exact fixed-point compiler
  and has passed a real clean-profile activation/server/diagnostics test;
- code is licensed under 0BSD; specifications, documentation, metadata,
  diagrams, and dedicated creative assets use CC0-1.0; and
- Linux and freestanding remain optional future targets and are not claimed by
  this release.

The repository-pinned previous OpenC compiler is used only to rebuild the
current OpenC compiler on a clean runner. The byte-identical rebuilt compiler
then performs the complete native workflow and release proof itself. D,
TinyCC, and generated C are not invoked anywhere in this release workflow.

Independent review remains invited and tracked honestly. No independent review
is claimed by this owner-maintained initial release.
